messages:
Jordan P: Hey all, day 2 and trying to run a streaming smoke test. I'm on a corp network with strict egress. Which key should I use (sandbox vs hosted) and how do people handle IP whitelists for the API? Also worried about accidental rate-limit storms from my test harness.

Rae (DevEx): welcome Jordan! :tada: Use the sandbox key for local dev/tests. Hosted keys are for staging/prod only. Sandbox keys are free but have lower quotas by default. Grab one from Console -> API Keys.

Rae (DevEx): common patterns for strict networks: 1) run the local devproxy which routes through our org egress IP (preferred), 2) use an SSH tunnel into a bastion in the office VPC, or 3) if you're an enterprise tenant we can arrange a dedicated egress block.

InfraBot: Note: sandbox default = 50 req/min and 6 concurrent streaming sessions per key. For larger tests open an infra ticket with expected qps and time window.

Jordan P: thanks — does devproxy require a ticket? can i run it locally without exposing my corporate IP?

Tom S: devproxy can be run two ways. Local dev (no org egress):
```
docker run -e RW_API_KEY=sandbox_ABC123 -p 8080:8080 redwood/devproxy:stable
# point app to http://localhost:8080
```
This still uses your local IP. If you need traffic to appear from the org egress (for whitelist), request devproxy access from infra and we'll give you creds to use the org-forwarder: it will egress from 35.227.44.200 (share this IP with security).

Priya - Security: FYI if you ask for the org egress IP to be whitelisted, please include the service tag and test window. We prefer temporary CIDR whitelists for dev tests.

Jordan P: great. Also, any tips on avoiding 429s while load-testing? my harness ramps quickly.

Rae (DevEx): yes — do staged ramps and respect the Retry-After header. Use exponential backoff + jitter. For token-based streaming, pace by tokens/sec and monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining/X-RateLimit-Reset headers. If you want, paste your script and we can recommend specific batch sizes.

Tom S: example curl with header check (quick):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sandbox_ABC123" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' \
  | grep -E "Retry-After|X-RateLimit-Remaining|X-RateLimit-Reset"
```
If you see Retry-After, back off that many seconds before retrying. For parallel streams, cap concurrency to avoid hitting the per-key streaming cap.

Jordan P: super helpful. I'll run a small ramp and share logs. If i need a temporary bump, what's the SLA for infra tickets?

InfraBot: Infra target response for temporary sandbox quota bump requests = 24 hours (business hours). Include start/end time, expected rps, and team contact.

Rae (DevEx): tag @infra in the ticket and cc me. We can fast-track small test bumps. Also if you're running CI tests, use ephemeral CI keys tied to the job so you don't leak long-lived keys.

Jordan P: noted. I'll try local devproxy first and open a ticket if needed. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
